title: Reversal Amount on a Refund Without a Return
content:
**Clause.** On any membership of Northgate Rewards and Northgate+ Memberships, the refund this schedule settles is the most recent refund without a return made because an item was damaged on arrival or never received on the member's Northgate orders, the one with the latest refund date and, among refunds of one kind on that date, the one recorded first, and when a damaged-on-arrival refund and a never-received refund share that date, the damaged-on-arrival refund; the earning it reverses is the Northgate Cash earning that points to the refunded line, and when no such refund is recorded or no earning points to that line, nothing is reversed.

The unreturned refund reversal is the reversal share multiplied by one less the relief fraction, rounded half up to the cent. The reversal share is the earned amount multiplied by the merchandise refunded on the refund, divided by the earning's basis (the earning basis recorded on that earning). The relief fraction is zero.

**Owed or not.** A reversal is owed on the refund this schedule settles when the earning basis recorded on the Northgate Cash earning that points to its line differs from that line's kept-units basis, and otherwise nothing is reversed. The kept-units basis is the line's net amount multiplied by the units kept (the units bought less every unit refunded without a return on the line), divided by the units bought and rounded half up to the cent, less the merchandise refunded on every return of the line. A line's net amount is the amount charged for the line after item promotions and the Northgate Card discount. Each refund record reverses cash at most once, and nothing is reversed when nothing was refunded.

**Worked example (hypothetical line of 2 units, net amount 140.00, earning 2.80 recorded on a basis of 140.00)**

| Step | Value |
|---|---|
| refund without a return of 1 unit, repaying | 70.00 |
| kept-units basis | 140.00 multiplied by 1, divided by 2, that is 70.00 |
| recorded basis 140.00 against 70.00 | they differ, a reversal is owed |
| reversal share | 2.80 multiplied by 70.00, divided by 140.00, that is 1.40 |
| reversal | 1.40 multiplied by one less zero, that is 1.40 |

Had the earning been recorded on a basis of 70.00, the two bases would agree and nothing would be reversed.
